land.text: Ifriqiya: 'eastern Algeria, Tunisia, and Tripolitania', territory the page calls 'not demarcated'

predecessors.note: In 800 'the Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Rashid appointed Ibrahim I ibn al-Aghlab' as hereditary emir; the dynasty ruled 'nominally as vassals of the Abbasid Caliphate'. Cliopatria has no shape for Ifriqiya 763-799 (the Fihrids and the Kharijites end in 762), so the land comes from no Cliopatria row.

land.text: Ifriqiya from Raqqada to the Zab, and Sicily

successors.note: 'On 25 March 909 Abu Abdallah entered Raqqada'; the Muslim conquest of Sicily page: 'Sicily passed under the Fatimid Caliphate' in 909. Cliopatria keeps the Aghlabid row to 910 and starts the Fatimids in 911.

capitals.name: al-Abbasiyya (Kairouan)
capitals.note: 'Al-Abbasiyya was founded outside Kairouan in 800 and built between 801 and 810.'

capitals.name: Raqqada (near Kairouan)
capitals.note: 'Raqqada became the capital in 876, when Ibrahim II moved there.'

capitals.name: Tunis
capitals.note: After 27 July 903 Ziyadat Allah III took power, 'basing himself in Tunis'.

capitals.name: Raqqada (near Kairouan)
capitals.note: 'In 907, Ziyadat Allah III returned his court to Raqqada'; Abu Abdallah entered it on 25 March 909.

union.text: the Libyan part of the Rustamid outline, Jebel Nafusa and south

correction.text: the Cliopatria Aghlabid shape plus the Jebel Nafusa of Tripolitania, held until the settlement of 812

keyframe_review.note: Valid 800-811 with the Jebel Nafusa added. The Aghlabids page gives Ibrahim's territory as 'eastern Algeria, Tunisia, and Tripolitania'; the Rustamid page has the Rustamid imam supporting the Huwara 'in their siege of Tripoli, which the Aghlabids held' in 812 and the Aghlabid emir 'ceding Tripolitania' in the settlement. Cliopatria draws the Libyan part of the Rustamid outline as Rustamid from 778, so the Aghlabid shape (246,406 km2, bbox to 18.9E) stops short of it; the Rustamid dossier cuts the same land out of its own shape for 777-811. No area figure in the infobox to compare.

correction.text: the 800 shape unchanged: Ifriqiya without the Jebel Nafusa, from the cession of 812

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 812-829: the 800 shape unchanged, after the cession of the Jebel Nafusa to the Rustamids in 812 ('made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania'; the page gives the siege year 812, the peace may fall as late as 817). The 824-827 revolt of the jund is a war, not a border change.

union.text: the Val di Mazara, the western third of Sicily

correction.text: the 830 shape plus the Val di Mazara, from Palermo's surrender in September 831

keyframe_review.note: Valid 830-839 with the western third of Sicily added. 'Palermo ... held out for a year until September 831'; the western third (Val di Mazara) 'fell relatively quickly into Muslim hands'. Cliopatria's shape adds only two cells (about 800 km2) at Palermo and Mazara.

union.text: the Val di Mazara, the western third of Sicily

correction.text: the 840 shape plus the Val di Mazara and Messina

keyframe_review.note: Valid 840-849 with western Sicily and Messina added. Taranto 'seized' in 840 is already in the shape (2 cells); 'In late 842 or 843 ... the Muslims' conquered Messina. Bari (847) was taken by Khalfun, an Aghlabid mawla, and is not Aghlabid land (Bari page).

union.text: the Val di Mazara, the western third of Sicily

correction.text: the 850 shape plus the Val di Mazara and Messina

keyframe_review.note: Valid 850-858: the 840 correction. Cliopatria's separate Emirate of Sicily row begins in 850 with 6,282 km2, smaller than the western third and Messina the pages give; that row's 860 step (18,935 km2) matches Enna's fall in January 859. The one Bari cell in the shape belongs to Khalfun's emirate.

correction.text: the 860 shape plus Sicily without the Byzantine east coast

keyframe_review.note: Valid 860-865 with most of Sicily added: 'in January 859, the Muslims scored a major success' at Enna, which 'reduced the Byzantines to the eastern coastal strip between Syracuse and Taormina'. Cliopatria's Emirate of Sicily 860 shape (18,935 km2) is that outline; it is used here, so the Sicily dossier should draw the island as Aghlabid land (governors sent from Kairouan) rather than as a separate state.

correction.text: the 866 shape plus Sicily without the Byzantine east coast

keyframe_review.note: Valid 866-869 (Sicily as in 860); new keyframe 870 adds Malta. Bari fell to Louis II in February 871 (Bari page).

correction.text: the 866 shape plus Sicily and Malta

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 870-874: Malta added: 'the capital Melite fell on 29 August' 870. Cliopatria's Emirate of Sicily 870 shape includes Malta (one cell).

correction.text: the 875 shape plus Sicily and Malta

keyframe_review.note: Valid 875-877: Sicily and Malta as in 870; Syracuse still Byzantine ('the Arabs finally, on 21 May 878, stormed the city'). Taranto's two cells stay (the Bari and Aghlabid pages are silent on its end).

correction.text: the 875 shape plus Sicily and Malta with Syracuse

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 878-895: Syracuse stormed on 21 May 878, the Byzantines reduced to the north-eastern strongholds (Taormina to 902). Cliopatria's Emirate of Sicily 878 shape (22,528 km2) is used.

union.text: the Libyan part of the Rustamid outline, Jebel Nafusa and south

correction.text: the 875 shape plus Sicily, Malta and the Jebel Nafusa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 896-899: the Jebel Nafusa won back from the Rustamids. The Rustamid page says only that the Rustamid area shrank to Tahert 'by the 880s' and is silent on 896; the year is taken from the Rustamid dossier of this project (Battle of Manu, not opened here), so confidence 1.

union.text: the Libyan part of the Rustamid outline, Jebel Nafusa and south

correction.text: the 900 shape plus all of Sicily, Malta and the Jebel Nafusa, to 25 March 909

keyframe_review.note: Valid 900-909, not 910: Taormina, the last Byzantine town, 'fell on 1 August' 902, which the page calls 'the effective end of Byzantine Sicily'; all of Messina province is therefore in from 902 (Taormina stayed Byzantine in 900-901). The 900 shape drops Sicily altogether (bbox top 37.3N, the same cells as 800) though the Aghlabids held it to 909. The dynasty ends 25 March 909, so the Cliopatria year 910 belongs to the Fatimid 911 row.

union.text: the Libyan part of the Rustamid outline, Jebel Nafusa and south

region.text: Ifriqiya: eastern Algeria, Tunisia and Tripolitania

ledger.note: 800: Ibrahim I ibn al-Aghlab becomes hereditary emir of Ifriqiya. 'In 800, the Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Rashid appointed Ibrahim I ibn al-Aghlab'; his territory 'covered eastern Algeria, Tunisia, and Tripolitania' and 'was not demarcated'; he founded al-Abbasiyya outside Kairouan that year. The page gives no month.

region.text: the Libyan part of the Rustamid outline, Jebel Nafusa and south

ledger.note: 812: Tripolitania ceded to the Rustamids. 'In 812, Imam Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Rahman supported the Huwara in their siege of Tripoli, which the Aghlabids held'; 'Emir Abdallah ibn Ibrahim made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania.' The page dates the siege to 812; the peace may fall to 817 (Abdallah's reign), and Tripoli itself stayed Aghlabid in Cliopatria's shape. Mirrors the Rustamid dossier's 812 gain.

region.text: Kairouan and its country, held by the rebel jund

ledger.note: 824: the jund revolt takes Kairouan. 'Under Ziyadat Allah I (r. 817-838) came a revolt of Arab troops (the jund) in 824'; the rebels took Kairouan in September, and their leader Mansur ibn Nasr al-Tunbudhi was killed about a month later. A rebellion of troops, not a state.
827: the revolt crushed. 'The rebellion was crushed in 827', and the conquest of Sicily began 'soon after Ziyadat Allah defeated the rebellion'.

827: the Muslim conquest of Sicily begins. 'On 14 June 827, the allied fleets sailed from the Bay of Sousse' under the commander Asad ibn al-Furat and landed at Mazara; Syracuse was besieged and the siege lifted in 828. The whole island is the zone; the gains below narrow it until Taormina falls in 902.

region.text: the Val di Mazara, the western third of Sicily

ledger.note: 831: Palermo falls. The city 'held out for a year until September 831', when its commander surrendered it; it becomes the Muslim capital of the island, and the western third (Val di Mazara) 'fell relatively quickly'. The first Aghlabid governor, Abu Fihr, arrives in Palermo in March 832.

840: Taranto seized. 'The Muslims seized Tarentum' in 840; the Aghlabids page puts the first major expeditions to the peninsula between 835 and 843, Amantea in 839 or 846 and Bari in 840 or 847. The pages do not say how long Taranto was held.
843: Messina conquered. 'In late 842 or 843, with Neapolitan support, the Muslims' took Messina; the Aghlabids page has 'captured in 842 or 843'.

847: Khalfun takes Bari. The Bari page: 'about 847 AD, when Kalfun (Khalfun), a mawla of the Aghlabid Emir of Africa, took Bari from the Byzantines'; it adds that the conquest was carried out 'without the support of any other Muslim state' and that Khalfun's successor was recognised as wali by the Abbasid caliph. Whether the Aghlabids were suzerain is not stated: client status is the researcher's bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: Sicily without the Byzantine east coast: Enna and the interior

ledger.note: 859: Enna falls. 'In January 859, the Muslims scored a major success' at Enna; it 'reduced the Byzantines to the eastern coastal strip between Syracuse and Taormina'. The region is Cliopatria's Emirate of Sicily 860 outline, which fits the page's description.
870: Malta conquered. 'The capital Melite fell on 29 August' after a fleet was sent in 870; the Aghlabids page: 'the Aghlabids conquered the island of Malta in 870'.
871: Bari falls to Louis II. 'In February 871, the citadel fell and Sawdan was captured and taken to Benevento in chains.'
876: Ibrahim II moves the capital to Raqqada. 'Raqqada became the capital in 876, when Ibrahim II moved there.'
878: Syracuse stormed. 'The Arabs finally, on 21 May 878, stormed the city.' The region is the step between Cliopatria's Emirate of Sicily shapes of 870 and 878.

region.text: the Libyan part of the Rustamid outline, Jebel Nafusa and south

ledger.note: 896: the Jebel Nafusa won back from the Rustamids. Battle of Manu, '3 or 4 May 896' (infobox; 'early May 896' in the text), an 'Aghlabid victory' of Ibrahim II over the Nafusa near the fort of Manu, west of Sabratha; the defeat 'marked the end of Rustamid rule over' the mountains. The page does not say the Aghlabids took direct control (the Nafusa kept their own governors), so confidence 2. Reviewer af-02-c: source and confidence raised from the Rustamid page at confidence 1, matching rustamid-dynasty /ledger/3.

902: Mila falls to the Fatimid movement. 'In 902 Ibrahim II became the only Aghlabid emir to personally lead a military campaign in Sicily' and on the mainland; 'While he was away, Mila fell to the Fatimid movement.' He died in October 902 besieging Cosenza (Aghlabids page). The Fatimid movement began among the Kutama in 893.
902: Taormina falls and Byzantine Sicily ends. 'Left unsupported by the imperial government, the town fell on 1 August'; the page calls it 'the effective end of Byzantine Sicily'.
902: Taormina, the last Byzantine stronghold, taken on 1 August; the Messina country is whole.
903: Ziyadat Allah III takes power on 27 July after Abdallah is assassinated and 'bases himself in Tunis'.
904: Setif falls to the Fatimid movement in October or November.
907: the court returns to Raqqada; 'Baghaya fell to the Kutama that year'.
907: Baghaya falls to the Kutama, the Fatimid movement.

region.text: Ifriqiya and Sicily at the Aghlabid fall

ledger.note: 909: the Aghlabids fall. 'On 25 March 909 (Saturday, 1 Rajab 296), Abu Abdallah entered Raqqada'; Ziyadat Allah III had already fled toward Egypt after the defeat at al-Aribus on 18 March. Sicily passes to the Fatimids the same year (Sicily page). Cliopatria keeps the row to 910.

wars.name: Revolt of the jund
wars.outcome: Crushed in 827; Mansur killed about a month after the rebels took Kairouan in September 824.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Sicily
wars.outcome: Aghlabid victory: Palermo September 831, Messina 842/43, Enna January 859, Malta 29 August 870, Syracuse 21 May 878, Taormina 1 August 902; Sicily passes to the Fatimids in 909.
wars.note: The Sicily page has the western third falling 'relatively quickly' in the early 830s but gives no other year for it.

wars.name: Aghlabid-Rustamid frontier wars

zones.text: the Libyan part of the Rustamid outline, Jebel Nafusa and south

wars.outcome: Siege of Tripoli 812 and the cession of Tripolitania; Ibadi tribes on the Aghlabid border rebel after 812 (undated); the Jebel Nafusa is won back in 896 (year from the Rustamid dossier).
wars.note: The page says the Rustamids held the Aurès and Zab only spiritually while they were 'nominally under Aghlabid rule'.

wars.name: Aghlabid raids on southern Italy and the Emirate of Bari
wars.outcome: Taranto seized 840, Bari taken by an Aghlabid mawla about 847; Louis II's coalition takes Bari in February 871. The Aghlabids' own role after 840 is not stated by the Bari page.
wars.note: Rome was raided in 846 and a naval battle at Ostia in 849 halted the advance (Aghlabids page); not territorial.

wars.name: Tulunid attack on the Aghlabids
wars.outcome: 'Under Ibrahim II (875-902), the dynasty faced a Tulunid attack and a Berber revolt' (Aghlabids page). The Tulunids page has Ahmad ibn Tulun take Barqa in 871 and put down its revolt in 875 but never mentions the Aghlabids, so the attack is undated and moved no border.
wars.note: Dates are the reign's bounds, not the attack's.

wars.name: Fatimid (Kutama) conquest of Ifriqiya

zones.text: Mila, Setif and Baghaya, then Raqqada

wars.outcome: The Kutama movement began in 893; Mila 902, Setif October-November 904, Baghaya 907, the battle of al-Aribus 18 March 909 and the entry into Raqqada on 25 March 909 ended the dynasty.

certainty.note: The Aghlabids page calls the territory 'not demarcated'; the Zab, Aurès and Tripolitanian frontiers with the Rustamids are tribal and move with allegiance; the Sicilian frontier moves by siege from 827 to 902 and is sharp only at the sea.

sources.title: Aghlabids
sources.note: Identity, capitals, territory, the revolt of 824, the Sicilian and Italian expeditions, the Fatimid movement and the fall in 909; no area given in the infobox.

sources.title: Muslim conquest of Sicily
sources.note: Dated steps of the conquest 827-902 (Palermo, Messina, Enna, Malta, Syracuse, Taormina) and the Fatimid takeover in 909.

sources.title: Emirate of Bari
sources.note: Khalfun, a mawla of the Aghlabid emir, takes Bari about 847; Bari falls in February 871.

sources.title: Rustamid dynasty
sources.note: The 812 Tripolitania settlement, the Rustamid extent and the 909 Fatimid conquest of Tahert.

sources.title: Tulunids
sources.note: Tulunid western frontier (Barqa 871 and 875); the page never mentions the Aghlabids.

sources.title: Battle of Manu
sources.note: Added by reviewer af-02-c: the 896 Aghlabid victory over the Nafusa that ended Rustamid rule in the Jebel Nafusa.

notes: Cliopatria's Aghlabid row is the Ifriqiya core plus a few cells at Palermo, Mazara, Taranto and Bari; Sicily from 850 is drawn in the separate 'Emirate of Sicily' row (850-910) whose steps at 860, 870 and 878 match the page-dated Enna (January 859), Malta (29 August 870) and Syracuse (21 May 878). The keyframes here reuse that row, so the Sicily dossier (eu-13) should draw the island as Aghlabid land until 25 March 909 (governors sent from Kairouan; 'Sicily passed under the Fatimid Caliphate' in 909) or the two rows would claim the same cells; the Emirate of Sicily row also has a gap 911-959. Bari 847-871 was founded by an Aghlabid mawla but recognised by the Abbasids (Bari page); Cliopatria's single Bari cell in the 850-874 shapes is kept in the Aghlabid shape, and a client relation is recorded at confidence 1. Taranto (two cells in the 840-899 shapes): seized in 840, end of Muslim rule not on any page opened. Reggio was captured on 10 July (901 by context) and Cosenza besieged in 902; retention is not stated, so neither is drawn. Pages disagree or are thin: the Rustamid page's 'ceding Tripolitania' is undated (812 siege, peace under Abdallah, 812-817); the Aghlabid page gives 909 for the fall while Cliopatria gives 910; Sardinia and Corsica occupations are disputed ('limited and inconclusive', Aghlabids page) and not drawn; the Zab, Biskra and Mzab are not named on the page. Counterparts without a dossier: the Kutama/Fatimid movement before 909 (loss events use fatimid-caliphate); the Emirate of Bari 847-871 (name used as the counterpart); the revolt of the jund is not a state. The 896 gain and its mirror in the Rustamid dossier rest on the Battle of Manu, a page not opened here (page budget). Rulers: the pages opened give Ibrahim I (800), Ziyadat Allah I (817-838), Abdallah ibn Ibrahim (812-817), Ibrahim II (875-902) and Ziyadat Allah III (903-909) but no complete list, so none is entered. Method note: every page was read through WebFetch, which returns a model-made extraction; phrases in quotation marks are the extraction's wording of the page and may differ in small ways from the live text, while the years and months are the ones it reported.
